value.body: Cabin crew keep passengers safe on board and look after them through the flight. Airlines hire them on domestic and international routes. A duty day includes a pre-flight briefing, safety checks, boarding, in-flight service and handling anything unexpected, from medical events to emergencies.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: Class 12 pass, through an airline's own selection

items.label: Training
items.value: Airline initial training under DGCA rules
items.note: Safety, emergency procedures, first aid and service

items.label: Domestic air passengers
items.source: DGCA annual domestic traffic data (as reported)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Apply to airline openings and attend selection rounds — screening, grooming and communication assessment, interview and medical. Selected candidates go through the airline's initial training before flying. Each airline sets its own age, height and other standards.

value.title: At a glance
items: Irregular rosters, overnight stays and time away from home are part of the job.
Next roles: senior crew, cabin supervisor, trainer, or ground and hospitality roles.
Fitness and medical standards apply throughout the career.

value.title: Domestic air passengers
value.note: Calendar-year passengers on domestic flights; 2021 was still affected by Covid-19. Passenger growth is one driver of airline hiring, not a count of cabin crew jobs.
value.source: DGCA annual domestic traffic data (as reported)
